headline_marked: Trump [[invites Putin to G20 summit]] in Miami
headline: Trump invites Putin to G20 summit in Miami
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the invitation is an opportunity for the Russian leader to engage with world leaders as Washington seeks to end the Ukraine war.
details: President Donald Trump has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami this December.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed the invitation, stating that solving problems requires meeting with those you disagree with.
The move comes as the US struggles to secure a deal to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine, with Trump insisting he is working with both sides to stop the war.
Rubio also encouraged Moscow and Kyiv to reach an energy ceasefire, noting that both sides have expressed interest in a limited agreement involving energy.
Meanwhile, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told the UN Security Council that Moscow would not halt its 'special military operation' in Ukraine.
On the ground, Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure in Ukraine killed at least seven people yesterday, including two in Kyiv and a child in the Donbas region.
In Odesa, the captain of a cargo ship was killed in a Russian attack, part of a wave of strikes targeting commercial vessels to hit export revenues.
caption:
Trump invites Putin to the G20 summit in Miami. Can this move lead to a peace deal in Ukraine?

President Donald Trump has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami this December.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed the invitation, stating that solving problems requires meeting with those you disagree with.

The move comes as the US struggles to secure a deal to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine, with Trump insisting he is working with both sides to stop the war.

Rubio also encouraged Moscow and Kyiv to reach an energy ceasefire, noting that both sides have expressed interest in a limited agreement involving energy.

Meanwhile, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told the UN Security Council that Moscow would not halt its 'special military operation' in Ukraine.

On the ground, Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure in Ukraine killed at least seven people yesterday, including two in Kyiv and a child in the Donbas region.

In Odesa, the captain of a cargo ship was killed in a Russian attack, part of a wave of strikes targeting commercial vessels to hit export revenues.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[discusses trade and economic ties]] with Croatian PM
headline: PM Tarique Rahman discusses trade and economic ties with Croatian PM
summary: The two leaders met on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York to explore expanding bilateral cooperation in technology, education, and investment.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković held a bilateral meeting on Wednesday, September 23, at the UN Headquarters in New York.
The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
Both leaders discussed strengthening the friendly bilateral relations between Bangladesh and Croatia, focusing on the expansion of trade, investment, and mutual cooperation.
Key areas of emphasis included economic cooperation, skilled manpower, education, technology, and other promising sectors for mutual growth.
The two Prime Ministers also highlighted the importance of enhancing cooperation within multilateral forums, including the United Nations.
They agreed to increase coordination on international issues of common interest to further strengthen the partnership between the two nations.
caption:
Bangladesh and Croatia are looking to expand their economic ties. PM Tarique Rahman and Croatian PM Andrej Plenković met in New York to discuss a new era of cooperation.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković held a bilateral meeting on Wednesday, September 23, at the UN Headquarters in New York.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).

Both leaders discussed strengthening the friendly bilateral relations between Bangladesh and Croatia, focusing on the expansion of trade, investment, and mutual cooperation.

Key areas of emphasis included economic cooperation, skilled manpower, education, technology, and other promising sectors for mutual growth.

The two Prime Ministers also highlighted the importance of enhancing cooperation within multilateral forums, including the United Nations.

They agreed to increase coordination on international issues of common interest to further strengthen the partnership between the two nations.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
